long_biography.plain_text:
Anatoly Bondaruk was born in Koziatyn, in present-day Ukraine, in 1958. He trained as an electronics engineer at the Rostov Higher Military Command School and later graduated with honours from the Dzerzhinsky Military Academy. He spent eighteen years in strategic missile-force research and command roles, leaving as a reserve colonel before moving into business.

Bondaruk founded Selena in 1997 and built his commercial career around petrochemicals. Selena later acquired Polief, an unfinished polymer complex in Bashkortostan. He became its director general and then board chairman, overseeing strategy for terephthalic acid and PET production. Bondaruk also chaired Bashkortostan's chamber of commerce, entered its regional legislature and represented the republic in the Federation Council, serving on defence and security.

No facts were transferred from Anatoliy Bondaruk namesakes with different patronymics or birth dates.

He was born in Koziatyn when it was part of the Ukrainian SSR within the Soviet Union; the city lies in present-day Ukraine. Ukraine is therefore proposed in place of the record's Russian Federation birth-country value, without treating birthplace as evidence of Ukrainian citizenship.
